text: answer[math-3b3a0f69-open]: 31 For 26,000–26,999, the final three digits must sum to 4, giving \(\binom{6}{2}=15\) possibilities. For 27,000–27,999, they must sum to 3, giving \(\binom{5}{2}=10\). For 28,000–28,599, they must sum to 2, giving \(\binom{4}{2}=6\); numbers from 28,600 through 28,605 cannot qualify. The 25,180–25,999 range contributes none, since its final three digits already have digit sum at least 9. Thus, \(15+10+6=\boxed{31}\).
